title: 1.06 — Systems of Linear Equations in Two and Three Variables

questions.title: What is the solution to a system of two linear equations graphically?
choices: The point where the two lines intersect
The area between the two lines
The slope of the steeper line
questions.explain: The solution to a 2D system is the exact point (x, y) shared by both lines where they cross.

questions.title: If a 2D linear system has no solution, what is true about the lines?
choices: They are the exact same line
questions.explain: Parallel lines share the same slope but different intercepts, meaning they never touch and have no solution.

questions.title: What do you call a system of equations that has at least one solution?
questions.explain: A system is consistent if it has one or more solutions. If it has absolutely no solutions, it is inconsistent.

questions.title: Solve the system using substitution: y = 2x - 1 and 3x + y = 9. What is the value of x?
If elimination results in an equation like 0 = 0, what does this indicate?
choices: The system has exactly one solution at (0,0)
The system is inconsistent with no solutions
The system has infinitely many solutions
The math choice is impossible to determine
questions.explain: A true statement like 0 = 0 means the equations are dependent and represent identical lines, yielding infinite solutions.

questions.title: Geometrically, what does a single linear equation with three variables (Ax + By + Cz = D) represent?
choices: A flat plane in a 3D space
questions.explain: Adding a third dimension variable maps out a flat, infinite surface called a plane.

questions.title: What is the primary target strategy when starting to solve a 3D linear system algebraically?
choices: Eliminate one variable using two different pairs of equations to reduce it to a 2D system
Graph all three lines on a standard grid
Guess values for x, y, and z until they balance out
Multiply all three equations together directly
questions.explain: By choosing a target variable to eliminate across two separate pairs, you drop the problem down to a standard 2D system.

questions.title: Solve the 2D system: x + y = 6 and x - y = 2. Find the ordered pair solution.
questions.explain: Adding the equations eliminates y: 2x = 8 -> x = 4. Plugging x back in: 4 + y = 6 -> y = 2. The solution is (4, 2).

questions.title: If three planes in a 3D system are parallel to each other like sheets of paper, how many solutions are there?
questions.explain: Because parallel planes never intersect all at once at any common point, the system is inconsistent and has no solution.

questions.title: In a 3D system solution group, what is the correct layout format for the final answer?
questions.explain: Solutions in a three-variable system require values for all three dimensional axes, represented as an ordered triple (x, y, z).
